📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In case you missed it: The Hunting Wives star Brittany Snow is engaged to photographer and creative director Hunter Moreno, and if the news took you by complete surprise due to having literally no idea she was dating anyone, you’re not alone. Their relationship is extremely low-key—like, so low-key that they’ve only been photographed together on one or two occasions, and the only reason we, the people, first learned about their engagement is because Claire Danes was caught asking about it on a red carpet.

That stated, there are some cute details to go over, so keep reading for a full timeline of Brittany and Hunter’s relationship!

Brittany and her ex-husband, Selling the OC star Tyler Stanaland, announce their split after two-and-a-half years of marriage in a joint statement:.

In a recent development, “This decision was made with love and mutual respect for one another,” they wrote on Instagram (via People). “We have realized we need to take some time and make sure we are each living our most fulfilling and authentic lives. We started this journey as best friends and our relationship will continue to be a priority not only for us but for our dog Charlie.”.

Four months after announcing their separation, Brittany reportedly files for divorce, citing “irreconcilable differences.”.

Brittany and Tyler’s divorce is reportedly finalized five months after she filed.

Brittany makes an appearance on Call Her Daddy, where she tells host Alex Cooper, “It’s so weird for me to be single. I’m saying weirdly because it’s very easy for me to get in a relationship, and I’ve been actively trying to be alone and be with myself and just feel the feelings and not have to band-aid it with sparkly, shiny, emotional things.”.

She adds that she’s been “in and out” of some flings, but has been pretty much keeping the vibes casual.

Brittany and Hunter start dating—or, at least, that’s when they’re first snapped kissing by paps while walking a dog.

Brittany tags Hunter in these pics, seemingly giving him photo cred:.

Recent findings suggest that brittany demonstrates up at the The Beast in Me premiere, and red carpet footage seemingly catches her telling Claire Danes that she’s engaged. At least based on lip readers thinking Claire claims, “You’re engaged. When did that happen?!”.

Not long after, TMZ confirms that, yep, Brittany and Hunter are engaged after a year of dating!

It has been revealed that A source tells Us Weekly that “Hunter is an extraordinary guy. He’s a mental health advocate and just a salt-of-the-earth kind of guy. They are so happy together.”.

Another insider claims, “Brittany and Hunter are so private and low-key, they just started telling friends recently within the last few weeks. It happened about a month ago. It was low-key and private.” Apparently Brittany’s friends “love Hunter for her” and say, “He treats her well. They are both very low-key people.”.

Recent findings suggest that aaaand they’re Instagram official! Some snapshots of Hunter make their way into Brittany’s photo dump from a birthday getaway, including these sweet pics:.

The Instagram love continues. Swipe for some cute snaps of Hunter (including a blink-and-you’ll miss it video of him and Brittany smooching):.

A sneaky pic of Hunter is included in one of Brittany’s Instagram photo dumps:.

Brittany takes to Instagram to share another photo dump, which includes several cute pics and videos of herself and Hunter. A few of my personal faves:.

We’ve got ourselves a hard-launch! Brittany celebrates Hunter’s birthday with a gushing Instagram tribute, writing, “Happy birthday to my favorite person on the planet.”.

In a recent development, she continues, “I must have done something right to deserve someone like you. Everyone who knows you, knows you are sunshine in human form. This was the first picture we ever took together (we didn’t know it was being taken) and I’ve never stopped hugging you & laughing with you since. It’s my favorite place to be. I love u @huntermoreno.”.

According to recent reports, at long last, Brittany fiiiinally confirms that she and Hunter are engaged. During an appearance on The Drew Barrymore Show ahead of The Hunting Wives season 2 premiere, Drew asks Brittany about the engagement rumors, to which she responds, “You know what? For the first time, I’m gonna tell you, I’m gonna tell you. Yes, we’re engaged, yeah.”.

She adds, “I haven’t remarked it before. It’s okay. It’s not that big of a secret. I mean, like, who cares?”.

According to recent reports, love this for her! Stay tuned for updates.

Patek Philippe's Golden Ellipse Reimagines a Design Classic

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (254 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Elledecor

⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Above: Patek Philippe Golden Ellipse watch in white gold, $43,011, patek.com.
  • Few watches make the case for pure design quite as convincingly as the Patek Philippe Golden Ellipse.
  • For 2026 Patek Philippe returns to that formula with the Golden Ellipse (Reference 5738G-001).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Above: Patek Philippe Golden Ellipse watch in white gold, $43,011, patek.com.

Few watches make the case for pure design quite as convincingly as the Patek Philippe Golden Ellipse. Introduced in 1968, its distinctive shape was conceived around the golden ratio, the mathematical proportion found throughout the natural world and long associated with harmony in art and architecture. Neither round nor angular, the curves of the Ellipse have an elemental quality that elevates its simplicity. Despite origins rooted in Renaissance mathematics, the watch also has an unmistakable groovy ’60s elegance.

For 2026 Patek Philippe returns to that formula with the Golden Ellipse (Reference 5738G-001). A larger case gives the watch more presence on the wrist, and at just a hair under 6mm thick, it retains the sleek profile that has always been central to its appeal. Inside is Patek’s ultra-thin self-winding caliber 240, equipped with a 22K gold mini-rotor.

The Golden Ellipse’s ode to nature continues through its use of color. The olive-green sunburst dial—and coordinating calfskin strap—recalls a shade found almost everywhere in the landscape, from leaves and moss to deep forest tones, shifting from an earthy green to brighter grassy flashes as it catches the light. Against the cool white gold case, matching baton markers and slender cheveux-type hands keep the dial remarkably clean.

Nearly six decades after its debut, the Golden Ellipse remains a design classic: mathematics, nature, color, and restraint distilled in one resonant shape.

This story originally appeared in the November 2026 problem of ELLE Decor.

20 White Elephant Gifts Everyone Will Fight Over

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • If you’re reading this, there’s probably a holiday gift exchange on your calendar coming up.
  • First, there’s likely a price cap, so we’re keeping everything under $100.
  • Luckily, that still leaves plenty of fun, affordable, crowd-pleasing gifts.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you’re reading this, there’s probably a holiday gift exchange on your calendar coming up. Maybe your boss organized one for the office, or maybe it’s the doing of that one friend who loves hosting so much they’d throw a party for Arbor Day. Either way, you’re probably wondering: What the heck do I bring to this thing?

There are a few rules to this game. First, there’s likely a price cap, so we’re keeping everything under $100. (If your white elephant involves luxury gifts, we’d love to be a fly on that very well-appointed wall.) Second, your gift should be something just about anyone would be excited to unwrap. That rules out clothes and shoes with specific sizes, phone cases for whatever iPhone model is right now in circulation, and franchise merch that assumes your giftee has seen every Marvel movie or follows football.

Luckily, that still leaves plenty of fun, affordable, crowd-pleasing gifts. We’ve rounded up our favorites below, so pick one, wrap it up, and take all the credit when everyone starts fighting over it.

According to recent reports, who doesn’t like waffles? A waffle-maker that’s easy to use and easy to store is for sure going to be a slam dunk at the gift exchange.

A cute felt ornament is a great gift that’s sort of holiday-themed, but also makes a fun gift for any occasion. It will take their Christmas tree to the next level—and even if they don’t celebrate Christmas, they can hang this little guy on a doorknob, at their desk, etc.

It has been revealed that jigsaw puzzles have always been a popular pastime, but people (ahem, my mom and sister) have especially taken up puzzling since the pandemic. Piecework makes some of my favorite puzzles, like this quirky peppermint-themed one.

Sources indicate that whether they drink coffee or tea, this leakproof tumbler will no doubt become their go-to drink vessel. Coffee for the morning commute? Check. Hot tea for an afternoon pick-me-up? Check. A glass of wine with dinner? Sure, why not. The Strova has all that covered (literally).

In these cold-weather months, hand cream is a must. This luxurious one from Homecourt smells like cedarwood smoke, sweet cardamom, cinnamon, and white leather.

Everyone wants a home that smells good. Aera’s aroma diffuser will make that happen. Yes, it’s at the upper limit price-wise, but it’s bound to be the gift everyone wants.

Just any old liquor won’t cut it, but Fords Sloe Gin is perfect for the holidays. Whoever gets this bottle will be making Sloe Gin Fizzes all winter long, and if you’re lucky, they’ll invite you over for one.

This rechargeable candle lighter is both practical and artful—it eliminates the need for matches altogether, and it looks classy next to a candle.

Yes, a candle is a classic gift exchange option, but don’t just go for your run-of-the-mill Yankee Candle; get one that will make their home smell like a winter wonderland.

In a recent development, who wouldn’t want a tiny printer that can instantly print photos from your phone? This one comes with a paper roll so your giftee can get started printing as soon as they open this awesome present.

Recent findings suggest that everyone needs a hat in the winter, so why not make it a nice cashmere beanie from Quince? They won’t know you only spent $35 on it—that’s how luxurious it feels.

This set of extra virgin olive oil and balsamic vinegar from Kosterina is a great gift for anyone who cooks, whether they’re a beginner or a professional chef. And the fun holiday packaging is a plus!

In a recent development, another thing everyone needs? A toiletry bag. No matter where they’re going this holiday season, they’ll need a place to pack their toothbrush, comb, razor, and whatever other bathroom essentials they use. Why not pack them in this cute pouch from Brooklinen?

Everyone is getting into peptides now. Make it easy for whoever gets this gift to start their peptide journey with this duo from Naturium.

Sources indicate that gloves don’t have to be boring. Verloop makes fun, colorful pairs that, yes, are touchscreen compatible. Everyone will want to get their hands on (and in) these.

A tiny record player that can actually play (tiny) records? It’s the dream of any music lover who lives in a small apartment!

It has been revealed that help someone get organized with a fun planner they’ll actually want to use. Burga has tons of cool patterns, so choose one you think will appeal to most people.

Sources indicate that A tote bag is the versatile catch-all bag everyone should have at least one of. And these mini ones from Steele are so cute and will last forever.

According to recent reports, if you’re going to go with a food gift, make it a Classic Panettone holiday cake from Eataly. Everyone will want a piece of this.

Pretty much anything from the MoMA Design Store is guaranteed to be a hit, and it will probably be the most unique gift at the party. Take these colorful crystal glasses, for example. Who wouldn’t want these in their kitchen?

Anne Hathaway is officially a mom of three, and her smile says she couldn’t be happier. Yesterday afternoon, the Oscar winner revealed to the world that she had given birth to her little one when she stepped out for a stroll in Fresh York City, smiling widely as she carried her newborn—a daughter—swaddled to her chest in a brown velvet baby carrier.

The only part of Hathaway’s youngest that was visible was her head, snuggled in a plum-colored beanie decorated with a tiny pink pom-pom, which peeked out from the top of the carrier.

In these first public photos with her newborn, Hathaway sported not only a big grin, but also a luxury gray overcoat from Brunello Cucinelli, which she layered over white sweats and a lavender knit sweater. She completed the cozy fit with brown suede Rothy’s clogs and a black baseball cap.

According to TMZ, who first broke the photos, the Verity star was seen walking around with a friend, who even stopped to capture snaps of Hathaway with her newborn.

Recent findings suggest that the Devil Wears Prada 2 star and her husband, Adam Schulman, are also parents to sons Jonathan and Jack, who were born in 2016 and 2019, respectively. Hathaway has yet to reveal when exactly she gave birth to their third child, or the name of their daughter, but the sex was revealed in a congratulatory Instagram Story by her costume designer, Molly Rogers.

After months of witnessing Hathaway’s incredible maternity style as she promoted her many projects of the year, we’re ready to be inspired by her mom fashion.

According to recent reports, saddles, stirrups, and horseshoes, oh my: We’ve been firmly in the year of the Fire Horse since February 2026, and the jewelry scene is officially in its horse girl era. Aside from the look being a clear classic in the world of jewelry (horseshoes were popular in Victorian-era jewels), today’s examples vary from sparkly creations to more minimal, toned-down pieces with everyday appeal. No matter the aesthetic, the jewelry of the Year of the Fire Horse is strong: This era only comes around every 60 years in the Chinese zodiac and is said to represent strength, independence, and fearlessness.

Celebrities are clearly fans: Taylor Swift just wore two double-layered horseshoe pendants to announce her Grammy nomination. Horse-ified jewelry also spanned the runway. For spring/summer 2027, both Gucci and Celine revisited the archival horsebit hardware detail and reworked it in a contemporary way to highlight the beautiful lines and sculptural symmetry of the timeless motif. Elsewhere, Chloé’s statement belt covered in huge running horses has been a fashion girl favorite and is the equivalent of jewelry for your waist.

There is perhaps nothing more classic than a chunky horseshoe ring or a horse-themed charm. Verragio and Oscar Heyman each reworked the symbol in gemstone-studded bracelets and double-motif rings. Elsewhere, Lionheart makes a slew of gloriously stunning oversize horse-head pendants and brooches brimming with diamonds and, sometimes, accessorized with mother-of-pearl saddles. The brand also partners directly with 13 Hands Equine Rescue, a nonprofit sanctuary located in Clinton Corners, Latest York.

It has been revealed that but this year, equestrian jewelry is not horsing around when it comes to experimenting. One such example is Hermès’s latest collection, which has an obvious horse connection: saddles, diamond-decked horse heads, and golden saddles. Titled “Into the Horsescape,” the 90-piece lineup is quite literally the horse girl’s dream: lassos in the form of massive baguette-cut diamonds and glimmering oversize horsebit bracelets replete with pavé brown and white diamonds. Pomellato also showcased a carved horse cameo surrounded by brown diamonds and suspended from a delicate rose-gold Dressage-link chain.

Industry observers note that if you want to lean into your inner horse girl in a more subtle, everyday way, Gucci’s iconic horsebit rings, refined drop earrings, and sleek bangles offer a sophisticated and versatile place to start your collection. Going vintage is another option: Equestrian themes have been reinterpreted in the jewelry space for hundreds of years now, so there’s ample opportunity. One thing is clear: Horse girl jewelry is galloping from the archives to the runway and into everyday style.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that it was just a few years ago that the balaclava was everywhere. Fashion people referred to it as the winter headpiece you absolutely needed. But now, I’ve noticed a new star, and that’s the snood, alongside the hooded scarf. Most people over the years have blended these three headpieces, but I’m here to inform the masses: you’re probably wearing a snood or hooded scarf now, not a balaclava.

Balaclavas are a full-coverage piece of headgear that wraps around the entire head, neck, and face (leaving only the eyes, nose, or mouth exposed), whereas a snood is a continuous circular loop or tube of fabric designed primarily to insulate the neck and cover the top of the head.

Balaclavas tend to be closer to the face, similar in fit to a ski mask, while snoods are loose-fitting and have a sort of cowl design to them. According to the winter sports community, balaclavas are better for skiing and extreme cold, but for most of us, we’re just looking to warm up a little with our winter accessories.

If you’re ready to wear your own snood this winter season, I’ve gathered some stylish inspo below to help build out those mood boards.

This brown snood moment with a light beige trench coat is peak winter outfit. The headpiece pulls the whole cozy vibes together and gives ultimate cool girl.

As a Floridian girlie, shorts in the winter are my kind of speed. Throw on those uber warm tights I see scrolling down my TikTok ‘for you’ page and you’re in business. The hooded scarf just elevates the whole moment too and keeps your head warm, which is ultimately the goal.

Colorful snoods aren’t always top of the list, especially if you’re looking for a headpiece that can blend with all your outfits. But if you’re hoping to bring a bit more fun to your winter style, then grabbing a snood like this one above is the way to do it.

Monochromatic is always in, but getting super close to a full black look and throwing in a light-colored headpiece is my personal winter hack. It brightens up the whole outfit, but doesn’t a neutral color like the one above still keep the look uniform and stylish.

Sources indicate that one of the most legendary entertainers in American history, Liberace dazzled audiences for decades with his over-the-top piano medleys, flamboyant costumes, and cheeky banter. The self-described “Mr. Showmanship” might be synonymous with Las Vegas, where he had a popular residency, but he also had a taste for Palm Springs, owning no fewer than four homes in the California desert oasis throughout his life.

Now, perhaps the most exceptional of those properties, a 1930s Spanish Revival estate—dubbed the Cloisters due to its network of arcades and courtyards—has hit the market for $6.9 million. Elsewhere in Southern California, the longtime Beverly Hills home of Hollywood power couple Annette Bening and Warren Beatty is also newly for sale, asking almost $15 million. And on the East Coast, Lady Gaga’s former penthouse atop Manhattan’s Hit Factory building is available for $7 million, while the most expensive home in Charleston just listed for $35 million. Check them all out below.

Acquired at the height of his career in the late 1960s, Liberace’s walled Spanish Colonial Revival estate in Palm Springs just hit the market for nearly $6.9 million. The famed entertainer turned the 1930s bed-and-breakfast, known as the Cloisters, into an extension of his opulent stage set, brimming with signature candelabras, opulent furnishings, and splashes of gold. He lived on the half-acre property until his death in 1987, after which upcoming owners have completely remodeled the 8,000-square-foot home to bring it back to its original splendor. HGTV host Brett Waterman spearheaded the most recent enhancement, filling the five-bedroom home with handcrafted details and understated furnishings. Perks include a heated in-ground pool, courtyards, and a spa facing the San Jacinto Mountains. It’s listed with Keith Markovitz and Rick Distel of TTK Represents at Compass.

Industry observers note that on Wednesday, ELLE Decor exclusively reported that the longtime Beverly Hills home of Warren Beatty and Annette Bening was hitting the market for the first time since they sold it. The Hollywood power couple custom-built the gated residence in 1992 and raised their four kids there, selling it in 2012 to hotelier Jonathan Baker and his wife, Jenny. They spearheaded their own revamp to the tune of $5 million, bringing a contemporary spirit to the interiors of the nine-bedroom compound, which includes a guest house, pool, and tennis court. Its new asking price is $14.995 million.

According to recent reports, last year, a 225-year-old mansion smashed the record for the most expensive home sold in Charleston, fetching a little over $21 million. Now, another estate is vying for the title. The Sword Gate House, located in the South Carolina city’s historic South of Broad neighborhood, just listed for $35 million with Leslie Turner of Maison Real Estate. Revamped by interior designer Cortney Bishop, the 17,140-square-foot mansion dates to the early 1800s and features preserved millwork, exposed brick, and an original mural in the dining room depicting historic Charleston harbor. There are also uncommon perks like a triple-decker piazza, a ballroom, a pool, and an acre of manicured gardens. The whole compound is secured behind preserved wrought-iron gates made by local ironworker Christopher Werner, giving the landmark its moniker.

Industry observers note that forget a “Million Reasons”—we’re looking at $7 million. The New York City penthouse where Lady Gaga once lived just hit the market for nearly $7 million—and she’s not the home’s only celebrity connection. The 3,700-square-foot duplex was also once home to former NBA star Carmelo Anthony and 30 Rock actor Tracy Morgan, per People.

In a recent development, with its organic silhouette, cantilevered roofline, and clever use of space, Leuthold House by Allan Gelbin bears the hallmarks of his mentor, legendary architect Frank Lloyd Wright. Completed in 1966 on five rolling acres in Fresh Canaan, the five-bedroom house spans roughly 5,700 square feet and underwent a restoration by Hobbs Inc. and JMK Architects in 2014. The interiors feature long expanses of glass and mahogany, while the grounds come with a spring-fed pond, a pool, a one-bedroom guest house, and 150 specimen trees. Listed for $6.2 million with John Engel and Melissa Engel of Douglas Elliman, the two-story house is on the market for the first time in 29 years.

Recent findings suggest that geoffrey Montes is an associate editor at ELLE Decor with a serious love for all things real estate and design. Before that, he worked at Architectural Digest, Galerie, and Preservation magazines, covering everything from jaw-dropping listings to world-famous architects and design events like Salone del Mobile and Homo Faber.

Doing my makeup, doing my hair, and then going to the closet and figuring out which three things in this entire room make sense together? You go through a fog. And fashion is so much fun, and I miss the fun.”.

It has been revealed that but at that point, she was getting back into dressing up. “Now I’m starting to just remember what I loved about it: the juxtaposition, putting the things together that don’t make sense,” she noted. “My fashion has always been driven by my mood, and my mood was on mom mode for a minute.”.

#43328. This Wood Finish Was Once Seen as “Outdated.” But Designers Now Say It's Coming Back.

📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Housebeautiful ↗ Open Full Page

This Wood Finish Was Once Seen as “Outdated.” But Designers Now Say It's Coming Back.

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1052 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Housebeautiful

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • For a period of time in the late 1980s to early 2000s, it seemed virtually impossible to enter a house and not come across honey oak.
  • “You’d see it everywhere—cabinetry, trim, stair railings, and floors.
  • However, there’s been a noticeable shift in the way people are wanting their interiors to look, and warmer spaces are definitely back in style.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For a period of time in the late 1980s to early 2000s, it seemed virtually impossible to enter a house and not come across honey oak. That bright, orange-toned wood finish covered kitchen cabinets, bathroom vanities, even baseboard trim and furniture around the house.

“You’d see it everywhere—cabinetry, trim, stair railings, and floors. It was the go-to wood tone for builders and homeowners alike,” Cathleen Gruver of Gruver Cooley tells House Beautiful. “But by the early 2000s, it started to fall out of favor as people shifted toward cooler, more neutral interiors.”.

However, there’s been a noticeable shift in the way people are wanting their interiors to look, and warmer spaces are definitely back in style. With this evolution, can we expect to see a revival of honey oak, as well? We asked a handful of designers if they think this golden wood finish is back, and how they would style it for modern-day interiors.

Elizabeth Bennett and Mallory Robins, the founders of interior design studio Kobel + Co, believe honey oak is back for two reasons: The first is that warm tones throughout the entirety of the home are on the rise; the second is that honey oak has a lot of nostalgic associations for people who grew up in the '80s and '90s and are now homeowners.

“We're seeing a resurgence of styles from this era not only in homes, but in fashion as well, as we harken back to a pre-digital era,” Bennett explains.

“It’s not necessarily a full-blown comeback, but I’ve definitely noticed a soft return—particularly in cabinetry, millwork details, and furniture," Gruver indicates. “Clients aren’t always asking for 'honey oak' by name, but they are gravitating toward natural wood tones that offer warmth and character.”.

According to recent reports, before you take a sledgehammer to those original honey oak cabinets, reconsider this tone by styling it in more modern ways. Keep reading to see fresh ways that designers are working with honey oak in their fresh projects.

As homeowners gravitate more toward lived-in, inviting interiors, honey oak is a wonderful way to add warmth. Leave it to the professionals to find stylish ways to make this once-outdated wood tone look cool again.

Industry observers note that plenty of designers will tell you to mix wood tones in your home to prevent it from feeling one-note, and the same is encouraged when honey oak makes a big presence. When designer Adina Hall took on the project above, there was too much honey oak in the space for her team to replace or refinish it all, so they embraced it instead.

“We developed a custom stain for the latest wood floors, a whitewashed French oak that created a neutral canvas for the structure without competing with the existing honey tone,” Hall states. “We added custom cabinetry finished in a taupe-tone ash veneer, again a neutral tone, and we leaned into crisp whites and some cool tones like sage green and indigo blue as accents to create a balanced palette.”.

Heavy amounts of warm woods can overwhelm the eye; it’s important to build a restrained palette and introduce interest with cooler tones, wood stains, sculptural furniture, and contrasting materials. “The key is to give the honey oak a contemporary context in order to make it feel like an intentional material that delivers a punch of warmth in an otherwise cool and architecturally bold yet restrained palette.”.

Whether you’re adding in fresh honey oak or you’re trying to work around what’s already in your home, one of the best ways to ensure it feels modern and not like a ‘90s Tuscan-inspired home is choosing an earthy color palette. Muted greens, warm whites, greiges, taupe, light blues—these are all beautiful hues that won’t add even more orange-ish warmth to your space.

Recent findings suggest that “Instead of making honey oak the focus of the room, I let the beauty of the wood shine through the use of clean lines, black matte touches, natural stones, and modern lighting,” designer Nancy Dow of Sierra Living Concepts says. She’s fond of using this wood, and uses these shades to create a modern and fresh appearance.

Industry observers note that rather than “wood drenching” a home in a single tone (as was often seen in the early aughts), Robins explains that current homeowners are exercising more restraint with their finishes. “Rather than the primary finish for a house on trim, floors, and cabinetry, it's being used in more subtle ways—a cased good piece or a kitchen island alone,” she states.

One of the reasons honey oak fell out of style is because it is a very warm tone, and in the world of “millennial gray,” an orange-tinted kitchen or bathroom isn’t very appealing. However, designer Marli Jones of Rebel House design studio believes this can be fixed simply by creating a contrasting palette.

Recent findings suggest that in the kitchen space above, Jones used only honey oak cabinetry in the scullery to contrast the light, bright main kitchen. “It adds a coziness to the scullery and envelops the space in warm, natural tones,” she claims. “That same honey color travels across the countertop stone and into the tile backsplash.” The two rooms are connected by the wall of glass and steel, but the change in materiality from the white cabinets to the honey oak creates a dynamic transition. “Warm wood always adds a grounding layer.”.

When adding a honey oak piece into your home, do so intentionally. Opt for a “stunning built-in, a custom island, or as an accent detail that brings texture and warmth,” Gruver indicates. To emphasize the styling, pair the honey oak piece with contemporary hardware or painted elements to help it feel fresh and curated.

While honey oak can work in any interior aesthetic, there are a few styles it looks best in, according to Gruver: updated farmhouse and cottagecore. Basically, “any space that leans into character, craft, and comfort,” she explains. However, she's also seen the tone used successfully in more modern, organic spaces where there's a large emphasis on natural materials and textures. It all depends on how it's balanced, which holds true for any wood tone. She adds, “When styled right, honey oak can absolutely feel current again.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Black Friday isn't until November 27, but that hasn't stopped mattress brands from getting a head start on the holiday savings. If your current bed has seen better days or you're waking up with more aches than you went to bed with, there's no need to wait until a designated shopping day to save big on an upgrade. We've spotted the 12 best Black Friday mattress deals to explore ahead of all of your Thanksgiving festivities.

Brands like Saatva, Birch, and Beautyrest are already offering up to $1,000 off on hotel-worthy innerspring mattresses, cooling hybrids, and organic options. Whether you're a side sleeper in need of a little extra cushioning for your hips and shoulders or someone who prefers a firmer, more supportive surface, there's something worth considering before the holiday rush kicks into high gear.

Below, you'll find AD-tested mattresses, complete with reviewer insights, notable features, and details about the current promotions. Get ready to find your next bed without losing sleep over the price tag.

Sources indicate that saatva is giving shoppers who have “luxury mattress” on their Black Friday wish list a head start on savings. The brand is taking over $600 off its popular Classic queen. Designed to deliver hotel-worthy comfort at home, the innerspring mattress features a dual-coil construction; a plush, three-inch Euro pillow top; and targeted lumbar support that helps promote spinal alignment. It also comes in three firmness options—plush soft, luxury firm, and firm—making it a versatile choice for different sleep positions. Reviewer Erin Kaplan, a combination side-and-stomach sleeper, praises the mattress's supportive feel, durability, and temperature regulation. “Overall, I get a better night’s sleep on a more consistent basis since I switched mattresses,” she claims. Complimentary white-glove delivery, a 365-night sleep trial, and a lifetime warranty round out the perks of this high-end buy.

Another name brand with an impressive 180 years of history, Stearns & Foster has a reputation for hotel-quality bedding you’ll find in luxury hotel chains like the Ritz-Carlton. They’ve already kicked off their Black Friday sale, which promises up to $1,000 off select adjustable mattress sets and a $300 Visa gift card with all mattress purchases. Senior visuals editor Melissa Maria raves about her Stearns & Foster Lux Estate Mattress, noting its seamless white glove delivery service was a game-changer. The level of firmness required an adjustment period for her, but the Tempur-Indulge memory foam layer and added pillow top gave it a more plush feel. “I’m a very light and finicky sleeper and it always takes me time to adjust to any sort of change, but my husband remarked at how well he slept and how much better his back felt after the first couple of nights sleeping on this mattress,” she indicates.

It has been revealed that beautyrest’s long-lasting mattresses are powered with advanced pocketed coil technology, helping couples with motion isolation and providing zoned support. The brand’s Black Friday sale is underway, and you can now save up to $1,000 on select mattress and adjustable base sets. Audience development manager Emma Tubbs recommends the Beautyrest Black Series One Mattress, which she claims has the “perfect firmness.” “As someone who continuously changes positions throughout the night, the quilted innerspring construction nicely accommodated my tossing and turning,” she writes in her review. “I often fall asleep on my stomach and move to my side and even my back as I fall deeper into REM—I feel supported by this mattress in each position.” Plus, the motion isolation has worked well for her, as she continues sleeping through her husband’s 5:30 a.m. wakeups.

Over the past century, Serta’s become known for making comfortable, solidly priced mattresses. As it stands, the brand is offering the lowest price we’ve seen in months on the Serta Five-Star Mattress. Shopping writer Julia Harrison had this mattress-in-a-box delivered downstairs, and managed to haul it up with the help of her roommate. She refers to it as relatively lightweight (thanks to the gel-infused foam versus a heavier gel bead layer), exactly medium-firm, and made without any frills. “Nothing about it feels too hard or too soft, which I know primarily because I never think about the density or firmness of this mattress (a good sign!) and because I’ve had no back or neck problems since sleeping on it,” she says.

Selecting a firmer mattress doesn't mean you’re opting for less comfort. That’s especially true with the original PurpleFlex bed-in-a-box, at the moment $100 off ahead of Black Friday. Unlike traditional memory foam beds, the PurpleFlex features a two-inch GelFlex Grid designed to relieve pressure while maintaining a supportive, responsive feel. Beneath that layer, a durable foam base provides stability, making the eight-inch mattress especially appealing to back and stomach sleepers who prefer sleeping on top of their bed rather than sinking into it. AD tester Chapin Rockwell particularly likes the firm construction, reporting “less back pain and stiffness” after switching to the PurpleFlex.

The WinkBed is a luxury hybrid mattress that caters to your preferred sleeping style, and it’s right now 30% off as part of the brand’s Veterans Day sale. What makes the WinkBeds particularly versatile is its four firmness options: Softer, Luxury Firm, Firmer, and Plus (the last level, Plus, is designed for sleepers who need additional support). Beneath its plush yet supportive Euro pillow top, pressure-relieving gel foam and individually wrapped coils work together to provide cushioning, targeted support, and motion isolation. A moisture-wicking Tencel cover also helps promote a cooler sleeping environment. But don’t just take WinkBeds’ word for it. Contributor Mark Burka notes that the mattress "provides strong edge support and wicks away heat," two features that help distinguish it from other hybrids. Moreover, it also comes with free shipping, a 365-night sleep trial, and a lifetime warranty, offering plenty of time to determine whether it's the right fit for you.

Industry observers note that side sleepers searching for a more supportive night's rest should put shopping Nolah's early Black Friday sale at the top of their shopping list. Shopping editor Audrey Lee, who tested an earlier iteration of the Evolution, praises its high level of comfort and cooling abilities. “I found this design’s contouring quality top-tier for pressure relief, but I still had ample support thanks to the coils,” she says. The brand is right now taking 35% off its mattresses, bringing the queen-size Evolution from $2,277 down to $1,480. Designed to cushion sensitive pressure points without sacrificing support, the luxury hybrid combines responsive AirFoam Luxe, individually wrapped coils, and targeted lumbar support to help keep the spine aligned. Shoppers can choose among Plush, Luxury Firm, and Firm options, all of which can accommodate an optional GlacioTex cooling pillow-top upgrade for additional cushioning and temperature regulation. A 365-night sleep trial, free shipping, and a limited lifetime warranty make the early holiday deal even sweeter.

To make your bedroom a little more environmentally conscious, consider starting with the Birch Natural Mattress, a medium-firm hybrid model that’s free of polyurethane foam, fiberglass, formaldehyde, and pesticides. Instead, it’s made from natural and organic materials, including breathable organic cotton, natural wool, and organic latex that’s certified by the Global Organic Latex Standard (GOLS), breathable organic cotton, and natural wool. Individually wrapped steel coils provide responsive support, while the latex offers gentle contouring (as opposed to the sinking feeling you might get from memory foam). Contributor Zoë Sessums was particularly impressed by the mattress's balance of softness and firmness, calling its feel "Goldilocks perfection." Birch Natural also features reinforced sides for additional stability that you’ll enjoy as you sit on the edge of your bed to put on your shoes. Free shipping, a 365-night sleep trial, and a limited lifetime warranty add even more appeal to the brand’s early holiday sale, which takes 25% off sitewide, bringing the queen-size Birch Natural Mattress down to $1,399 from $1,865.

According to recent reports, handcrafted in Illinois, this mattress combines three inches of GOLS-certified organic Dunlop latex for a breathable, responsive sleeping surface with organic cotton and wool that’s certified by the Global Organic Textile Standard (GOTS). (That’s a third party verification that ensures the organic origin and processing of the materials used in the bed.) The Natural Escape’s individually pocketed coil system features seven zones of targeted lumbar support, making the mattress a strong contender for shoppers who prefer a firmer surface. "I feel super supported," notes contributor Kristi Kellogg of her experience testing the Natural Escape. She also has zero back pain while sleeping on it and appreciates the straightforward delivery and setup process: It arrives compressed in a box and includes free shipping and returns, a 365-night sleep trial, and a 20-year warranty. Need another reason to consider making the switch? My Green Mattress is right now taking 10% off orders during its Go Green Sale, with the Natural Escape Organic Mattress queen going for $1,829, down from $2,079.

It has been revealed that just like the Saatva Classic Mattress, you can save up to $625 off when you buy an adjustable base or upholstered bed frame with this mattress. The luxury mattress is made with sustainable materials such as organic cotton and plant-based flame retardants. In fact, the eco-friendly construction even won over contributor Bailey Berg’s partner, an environmental scientist. It’s been four years since Berg brought the Loom & Leaf Mattress home, and she says it hasn’t lost its composure. “My partner and I joke about feeling like we’re floating on a seat of comfort,” she says. “There’s little to no sag. I think any kind of sleeper—side sleepers, stomach sleepers, and back sleepers alike—would like this supportive pick.”.

Sources indicate that we’ve all been there: You toss and turn, flip your pillow looking for cool relief, and feel disappointed when you find nothing of the sort. If you tend to overheat easily, Casper's early Black Friday sale could be your chance to finally get a less sweaty night's sleep. Designed to keep nighttime overheating at bay, the mattress uses Casper's Snow Technology, which combines a pleasantly crisp QuickCool cover, phase-change material designed to absorb and disperse heat, and aluminum graphite HeatDelete bands that help draw excess heat away from the body. The mattress’s zoned memory foam and supportive springs also provide cushioning and spinal support without the overly plush sensation of an all-foam mattress. After testing the Snow Hybrid, contributor Kate McGregor describes its feel as "squishy when I lay down," while noting that the foam doesn't make getting out of bed difficult. She also loves its motion isolation and cooling qualities, although there were some lingering off-gassing smells after unboxing. Really, the only hot thing about this bed is its early Black Friday Deal: the sale offers over $800 off the queen-sized hybrid mattress, making now a great time to buy.

Tuft & Needle is an Arizona-based retailer touting reasonably priced mattresses made with the brand’s cooling and pressure-relieving T&N Adaptive Foam Technology. Now, the prices are even better with the pre-Black Friday sitewide sale. Everything is 20% off, including the Tuft & Needle Mint Mattress. Contributor Anna Fixsen is a side sleeper who prefers a medium-firm feel, and states she’s met her match with the Mint mattress. “I fell asleep faster and better on this mattress than my old innerspring mattress—despite being someone prone to tossing and turning—making this a great option out of all the memory foam mattresses out there,” she writes in her review. She attributes her restfulness to the invisible support layer of cushy gel beads, providing a cool, supportive slumber.

I am the ultimate beauty Santa amongst my friends and family. Beauty gifts can be notoriously difficult to give—I mean, there are always questions of shade, hair type, skin type, and scent preferences. And for some, it might feel awkward to give someone, say, a wrinkle cream or foundation, no matter how fancy and expensive it is. But as a beauty editor, it’s basically my duty to give away the best beauty gifts every year. I’ve gifted LED masks, hair tools, high-end skincare, and even the odd designer nail polish or bodycare. Among it all, though, the most excited I’ve ever seen my family get is opening a box filled with Jones Road Beauty.

Created by makeup industry legend Bobbi Brown, Jones Road is makeup, but better. All of the brand’s products perform easily, with minimal fuss, making it a go-to for anyone who isn’t a whiz with a brush but wants to look like one. And it’s particularly fantastic for mature skin, thanks to creamy, moisturizing formulas that don’t cling to texture or settle into fine lines.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that personally, I’m thrilled that cool-toned makeup is making a comeback. I lived through the warm-toned trend, when it seemed like every palette featured varying shades of orange, orange, and more orange—none of which complement my fair complexion with pink undertones. Now, I’m taking advantage of the latest, cool-toned trend by enhancing my eyes with silver shadow, swiping on milky pink lip glosses, and even transforming my warm, summer blushes into flattering winter-ready shades with the help of the newly introduced SHEGLAM Squeeze & Dot Matte Paint Blush in Gray-tiful.

It has been revealed that yes, the blush is actually gray in the tube, but that isn’t as scary as you may think. In fact, it’s rapidly becoming the MVP of my makeup bag. Not meant to be worn alone, it’s designed to blend with other blush shades to neutralize bright colors, cool off warm tones, and help you customize the intensity of your blush. I can combine it with any of my cream or liquid blushes, including the rest of the shades in the fresh SHEGLAM Squeeze & Dot Paint Blush collection in matte and shimmer. Suddenly, I’m getting so much more mileage out of blushes that I used to only reach for during the warmer months, when my complexion is naturally sun-kissed and I feel more pulled toward more vibrant looks.

In a recent development, gray-tiful is one of eight Squeeze & Dot Matte Paint Blush collection, which also includes shades of peach, mauve, pink, and red. The formulas are infused with hyaluronic acid and glycerin to keep cheeks soft and hydrated. The squeeze-tube dotter makes it easy to pinpoint application exactly where I want it, whether that’s high up on my cheekbones, on the apples of my cheeks, or on my chin and nose for an all-over flush.

Here are my three favorite ways to use Gray-tiful, below.

Recent findings suggest that SHEGLAM Squeeze & Dot Matte Paint Blushes such as Chili Rouge, a candy apple red, and Love Cake, a bright pink, are impressively pigmented. For me, this makes them perfect for special occasions, but for running errands or casual hangs with friends, I prefer a softer look. When I mix them with a dot of Gray-tiful using a dense bristle brush, these bold shades become more subtle, which matches my low-key, everyday vibe.

There’s something so pretty and whimsical about a frosty cheek, especially in the winter. I like to apply two dots of the SHEGLAM Shimmer Paint Blush in the peachy Pink About You on my cheekbones, then add one dot of Gray-tiful, and blend. The result is a luminous, cool-toned flush that catches the light beautifully.

This has to be my favorite way to use Gray-tiful; I feel like an artist mixing up my own custom hues. This is a time for creativity and experimentation, so there’s no one right way to mix colors. I like to squeeze a dab of Gray-tiful on the back of my hand, then add one, two, or even three blush colors on top and mix them all together to see what I can create. Recently, I transformed the Matte Paint Blush in Heart Wish, a warm mauve with two dabs of Gray-tiful and the tiniest hint of Pink About You. The result? My dream winter blush shade.

It has been revealed that when it comes to the woman who has everything (aka your mom, wife, grandma, or mother-in-law), the last thing she needs is more meaningless stuff. What she does need (and definitely wants) is something thoughtful that highlights your love and appreciation. And now that it’s almost December, it’s really time to start thinking about the perfect holiday gift.

So what do you get for the woman who already has it all? Good question. Lucky for you, we’ve already handled the hardest part and put together a list of gifts any woman would want, no matter how full her closet already is.

Maybe it’s something romantic and personalized for your wife, like a luxury photo album filled with pictures of the two of you together; maybe it’s a flower or coffee subscription that will keep making her smile throughout the year. Or maybe it’s a newly introduced apron for the home chef, a digital photo frame for the faraway grandma, or a cashmere sweater that will keep her cozy for years to come. You could even go all out and get her a sparkly piece of jewelry you know she’ll wear every day.

In short, whichever special woman you’re shopping for, there’s something here that will make her holiday season extra special, all thanks to you.

In a recent development, A pair of statement earrings for under $300 is a no brainer, especially when they look as nice as these suspended round-cut ones from Dorsey. If she wants something more dainty, go with the petite size; for something more bold, you can opt for the oversized version. Or keep it classic with the medium. Whichever you choose, she’s going to be impressed.

It has been revealed that if you can swing a tennis bracelet that’s a step up from stainless steel and sapphire, it should be this one from Ring Concierge. With a choice of natural diamonds or lab-grown diamonds and 14-karat white gold or yellow gold, it is truly a luxurious and timeless piece.

A set of luxe pajamas from Petite Plume will give her the sweetest of dreams, and with more than 20 colors and patterns to choose from, there’s sure to be a set she’ll obsess over.

Recent findings suggest that made from vegan shearling, these fluffy slippers from Rothy’s are so cute and so comfortable, thanks to a cushioned footbed. Every day spent lounging around the house in these will feel like a luxury.

It’s a small but mighty gift that lets her bring a reminder of you wherever she may go. Personalize it with her initials for a special touch.

If she’s astrologically inclined, try this made-to-order birth-date book, which features an illustration of her unique astrological birth chart on the cover and a detailed analysis inside.

The Dyson Airwrap is the hair tool every woman wants. With different options for different hair types and six attachments, she literally won’t ever need another hot tool for the rest of her life.

Everyone is getting into peptides now, and the best introduction to that is with Dr. Barbara Sturm’s new peptide serum, which won a 2026 Esquire Grooming Award.

If she’s been talking endlessly about an upcoming weekend trip, you gotta get her the nicest weekender bag in the world, and that’s the Vérité weekender from Métier.

Don’t just gift her a perfume that smells good; get her something that will look good on her dresser, shelf, or wherever she keeps her fragrance. Bulgari’s latest Omnia Amethyste eau de parfum is a gorgeous woody floral blend that comes in one of the coolest bottles I’ve seen.

Whether she’s traveling or just likes to keep her stuff organized at home, Afform’s Traveller is the perfect system to keep all her makeup brushes and products tidy. It looks so nice I actually keep mine on my dresser all the time.

It has been revealed that A bottle of vintage Dom is for the lady who knows her bubbles. Like, really knows her bubbles.

So she’s looking for a new laptop? Make it the new MacBook Neo, Apple’s best-looking laptop that comes in at less than $1,000.

It has been revealed that nothing feels quite as luxurious as lathering yourself in Diptyque body lotion after a shower and before bed. This one has the brand’s famous rose scent, which she will fall in love with.

You can never go wrong with a diamond necklace.

When in doubt, go with something classic from Tiffany, like this 18k yellow-gold double-link bracelet.

Flowers are beautiful, timeless, and romantic—which is why they always make a great gift.

For a luxury watch that’s especially luxurious, go with Hermès. This dainty silver Nantucket watch will become her favorite latest accessory.

Industry observers note that if she’s a tea drinker like me, she’ll really appreciate a good tea gift set. We love this one from Forgrave, which includes black, white, green, and herbal blends and comes with the brand’s signature tea infuser.

Tech Report: Pink Hair Is Back and Everyone From SZA to Adéla Are Making a Case for It

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (922 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cosmopolitan

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that remember when Kylie Jenner was changing her hair color about every other week, Tumblr was overflowing with pastel-haired girlies, and we were all contemplating whether we could pull off pink hair?
  • In a recent development, and the range is range-ing.
  • There’s a truly pink hair color for everyone.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that remember when Kylie Jenner was changing her hair color about every other week, Tumblr was overflowing with pastel-haired girlies, and we were all contemplating whether we could pull off pink hair? Well, dust off your 2016 Pinterest boards, bb, because pink hair is officially making a comeback. But this time, it’s not just King Kylie leading the charge. SZA, Adéla, and even Martha Stewart have been putting their own spins on the color, proving that there’s no one way (or age!) to enter your pink hair era. “Since pink is not a natural hair color, you don’t really have to abide by any typical color analysis rules,” claims colorist Emily Claire, which means you have free range to do whatever the heck you’d like.

In a recent development, and the range is range-ing. From electric pink to soft rose gold, I promise there’s a rosy hue for you. Personally, I’m loving this return to hair color that’s just fun—and I’m not the only one. “Recently my clients with pink hair have been requesting baby pink and deep berry pink,” indicates colorist Cara Craig. Plus, Cosmo called out pink as a top fall hair color trend this year. So, whether you’re ready to go full-on Barbie or want to experiment with a subtle rosy tint, there’s a pink hair idea with your name on it. Ahead, we’re breaking it all down, including how to choose your shade, what to ask for at the salon, and how to keep your pink hair looking fresh.

Short answer: Yes. There’s a truly pink hair color for everyone. “I have clients asking for all shades of pink, from blush and rose gold to hot pink to magenta,” notes hairstylist Alyssa Chapa.

Pink is surprisingly so versatile, so there are plenty of ways to make it work for you. “In my opinion, pink is a neutral. I think of fashion colors as cousins to classic shades,” indicates Craig. “So if you are a blonde, consider baby pink. If you are a brunette you’ll want to move to darker pinks and fuchsias. If you want to feel like a redhead then wear rose golds and warm pinks.” She also recommends a violet pink if you prefer keeping things cool-toned.

Recent findings suggest that wondering about how your skin tone will look with pink hair? “I’m personally of the opinion that there is no right or wrong shade for your skin tone,” indicates Chapa, but if it’s really notable to you, here are her tips for finding the best hair color for your skin tone. “Start by figuring out your undertones,” she says. “I like using the veins on the inside of the wrist; if you have blue or purple veins then you usually have cool undertones, green veins mean warm undertones, and a mixture of both is a neutral undertone.” Then, it’s pretty easy from there: Match your undertones to the shade of pink, which your colorist will be able to help out with (think baby or icy pink for cool tones, peach or salmon pink for warm tones, that kind of thing).

Sources indicate that first things first: Bring reference photos to your colorist—we’ve handily included some pics throughout this story for ya. After all, Adéla’s vivid pink and Stewart’s subtle rose gold hair require very different approaches, so you’ll want to make sure you’re specific about what shade you’re after.

“For most people, unless you happen to be naturally blonde, the process would involve lightening your hair to the desired level with bleach, then toning it to the desired pink with a direct dye,” indicates Claire.

Industry observers note that need some specific pink hair ideas? These are colorist-approved: “One of my favorite ways to wear pink lately is over classic blonde highlights,” notes Craig. “I also love a pink double process (e.g. Adéla).” Double process just means a two-step coloring method—your colorist will first bleach/lighten your hair, then apply the pink color. You can also go with chunky highlights, “especially a halo hairline where the pink frames the face,” adds Chapa. “Mixing chunky pink highlights in with shades of red or brown to create a kind of calico effect is also popular online.”.

Now for the not-so-fun part: Pink hair doesn’t necessarily equal low-maintenance hair. “No matter the tone, you’re going to have to refresh it in four to six weeks if you want it to stay pink,” notes Chapa. If you want to go as low-maintenance as possible, a softer pink is the way to go, notes Craig.

For a more natural-looking grow-out or to keep your hair color easy, “your alternatives are to choose an already muted color like a dusty rose or mauve and let it fade to blonde or brunette, or to invest in an at-home color depositing treatment to maintain your pink until your next salon visit,” Chapa says.

You can help extend your color by washing less frequently, using color-safe shampoo and conditioner, limiting heat styling, and incorporating a color-depositing mask or at-home hair gloss. “I always recommend my clients use a pink-tinted shampoo or conditioner to keep up with the color between appointments at home,” says Claire.

The look works because it balances warm and cool. The rich brown base keeps things grounded and neutral, while the berry undertones add a soft flush of color that feels fresh rather than flat. It’s a shade that flatters nearly every skin tone, and it’s subtle enough for the office yet moody enough for a night out. For an extra touch, try a glossy top coat to mimic that just-dipped chocolate shine, or add a thin chrome or sheer pink accent nail for a little dimension.

From dreamy cotton-candy pink to a deep, jammy berry, these rosy shades capture every stage of a juicy strawberry, from first blush to fully ripe.

Soft pink polka dots float across a deep burgundy base, a playful nod to retro charm with a ripe, berry-rich finish.

This manicure features DND’s Strawberry Wine, a moody fall shade that’s hard to beat.

  • According to recent reports, in ELLE’s Office Hours series, we ask people in powerful positions about their first jobs, worst jobs, and everything in between.
  • I ran a camp in my neighborhood because, at the time, I thought I wanted to be an art teacher.
  • Industry observers note that I was always creative growing up.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, in ELLE’s Office Hours series, we ask people in powerful positions about their first jobs, worst jobs, and everything in between. This month, we sat down with Lafayette 148 creative director Emily Smith as the Fresh York-based fashion house celebrates its 30th anniversary. Smith has spent more than two decades at the helm of the brand, working her way up from a part-time freelancer to creative lead. But her fashion ambitions began long before she arrived in New York. Growing up in Atlanta, she ran her own neighborhood art camp before discovering designers like Donna Karan and realizing fashion could be a career. Now, Smith is celebrating the women who have shaped Lafayette 148 through its “Uniform” campaign, which highlights accomplished New Yorkers and their individual approaches to personal style. Below, Smith reflects on her unconventional start, why she’s stayed at the firm for over 20 years, and the career advice she wishes she’d followed sooner.

I ran a camp in my neighborhood because, at the time, I thought I wanted to be an art teacher. It was basically babysitting all the neighborhood kids, but I created a flyer, got paid for it, and did the whole thing. I started in second grade, and we did it every year for about eight years. I even started hiring people so we could have two classes going at once. We had swimming lessons. The local news even came and did a segment on it. I loved decorating my classroom and setting everything up. My parents were so nice to give me the garage and basement to do it all. Not necessarily an official job, but my first money-making moment.

I was a bagger at Kroger. It just was not for me.

Industry observers note that I was always creative growing up. At a certain point, I discovered Donna Karan. It’s kind of crazy when you see somebody doing something and suddenly realize, Oh, that’s a career. I can do that. I became obsessed with everything in the ’90s, all the Fresh York fashion at the time. That was when I decided I wanted to pursue it. When college applications came around, my mom really encouraged me to go to art school. I started in fashion, and that became my focus. Growing up in Atlanta, I wasn’t necessarily surrounded by a big fashion community. But my dad’s office was across the street from the art museum at one point, and I remember going there and having that exposure. My mom was always crafty and creative, too. She really encouraged us to be who we were.

It has been revealed that there’s a language creative people have that’s a little different from the way business people communicate. When I went to art school, I felt like I’d found my people. It wasn’t just fashion people. It was photographers, fine artists, and all these different kinds of creatives. Being around people who thought about things differently was really inspiring. Even today, I thrive around people who have creative insight. There’s always a little more depth to the way they see things.

I interned at Bill Blass for about six months. I moved to New York in July 2001, and we had our fashion show on September 10. I remember Marc Jacobs had his show that day, too, and everybody was celebrating. People were saying, “Just come a little late to work tomorrow.” And then, obviously, September 11 happened. A week later, the entire team was let go, from the top down. What I learned from that experience was the fragility of everything. Don’t take anything for granted. Anything can come and go in a moment. But I also worked with Lars Nilsson and Hervé Pierre Braillard, who were just the kindest people. This industry has a little bit of everything, but I loved that they led with kindness, even when they were under so much pressure. As an intern, I was literally carrying ironing boards down the street and doing a sketch here or there. It was very much about doing whatever needed to be done.

After my internship, I had a brief stint of freelancing. Those were some long months. I remember coming home from one job and my roommates asking how my day was. I noted, “Well, I was putting pigs on socks.” I knew I wouldn’t be going back. Freelancing is hard. It’s a grind, but you meet a lot of great people. I actually made some really good contacts during that time. I eventually met Deirdre [Quinn], Lafayette 148’s founder. She met with me on a Saturday, which I thought was incredible. I was really just looking for advice. I wasn’t looking for a job, and I didn’t even know much about the brand. It was only five years old. She was so kind, full of knowledge, and passionate. After I spent a year freelancing and meeting people who seemed so over the industry, her enthusiasm reminded me why I wanted to do this in the first place. She offered me a part-time freelance position, and the rest is history.

Recent findings suggest that in the beginning, security was really notable to me. The idea of losing a job and having to pay rent was scary, so that was definitely part of it initially. But really, it was the growth. Within a couple of years, they were sending me to the factory. It was a small, tight-knit firm, so I was able to wear a lot of different hats. I had a mentor named Barbara Gast who was traveling back and forth from Italy, and I was learning so much from her. I’d compare notes with friends in the industry and realize how much hands-on experience I was getting. I understood the value of that and really loved being so close to the product. It never got boring. And whenever things did get slightly boring, I’d ask, “Okay, what’s next?” And there was always something. It’s such an entrepreneurial place that you can almost create your next opportunity. That’s what made it so exciting.

I think if you asked Deirdre, she’d have a different answer because she has her own experience of building the tech giant. For me, it’s about having started at a company that was really a factory and being part of the journey of building its identity and what it stands for. I was the kid running up and down the factory floors collecting samples. That hustle and bustle was so innate to who the brand was. To me, it was really exciting to build more of a brand story around that. Thirty years later, we’re still celebrating those roots and making sure we haven’t strayed too far from them, while continuing to evolve. Being part of that journey has been really exciting.

Sources indicate that the constant has always been this idea of an accomplished woman. She’s always been at the forefront of who we’re designing for. At the time, it was the career woman. But now, what does that even mean anymore? What does that look like? There are so many different versions of that woman and so many different ways people dress. At the heart of it, she’s a woman who knows what she wants. She’s busy and has a really full life, whether she’s starting her career or ending it. They can all find something in the clothes.

For us, it was about choosing people who inspire us. Number one, they had to be Fresh York women. That was the base. We wanted women who make us want to be better ourselves. From someone like Deborah Berke, the architect, to women who have built incredible careers in other fields, it’s key to shine a light on them. I think back to when I was a kid and how much you need that kind of inspiration. Even at a certain stage in your career, when you’re wondering what the point is, it’s nice to have people who inspire you. These are women who have really built something for themselves, and I think that’s worth celebrating.

Industry observers note that sophie de Rakoff noted something during the project that I really liked, and I’m going to steal it: “Dressing with intention.” When you know yourself, you know what works on you. It’s no longer about dressing to impress. There’s a confidence in knowing what works for you and making it work. We’re all so busy. Who has time to overthink getting dressed? You know what works, and you build a system around that. You’re able to create a wardrobe that really works for you. Everybody has a different definition of a uniform, and that was the whole point of the project.

It has been revealed that when I first started in the industry, I was a total hippie. I was making my own clothes, and they were terrible. Absolutely falling apart. It was what it was. I think part of the change comes from not having as much time as you did when you were younger. But it’s also about simplicity and comfort. I know that if I’m going to be on the floor pinning something but also have to give a presentation, there are certain pieces that work for both. I can be comfortable and still feel appropriately dressed. I’ve found a handful of things that work for me, and I don’t have to think too much about them anymore. A crisp, oversize white cotton button-down is half my closet. I also love a soft skirt and a significant chunky sweater. Those are the pieces I always go back to and interchange depending on the day. I even wear sweaters in the summer. It’s cold in the Navy Yard!

Our pants fit incredibly well. The moment somebody gets into our pants, they’ll love us forever. Then it’s the jacket and the white shirt. Those three things are our gateway pieces, and everything else follows. You need a good blazer and a good leather piece, too. Once you find those foundational pieces that really work for you, everything else becomes easier.

Industry observers note that I really want to see more women in our clothes. It’s not just about growing the business. It makes me happy when I see people put on our clothes and feel really good. We work so hard to make sure things fit the way a woman wants them to fit. I just want more people to enjoy that.

This interview has been edited and condensed for clarity.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you, like most people, hear the term “bourbon chicken” and have no idea what it is, let me call it by its more common name: toothpick chicken. Yes, the suspiciously delicious chicken shelled out at mall food courts on toothpicks is most likely bourbon chicken. Popular at American Chinese or Cajun-style Chinese restaurants, the sticky-sweet chicken is the utter definition of delicious, luring weary shoppers into food courts to find refuge from the bubblegum pink sweatpants and ripped denim. This version takes cues from the classic but swaps in some autumnal ingredients to make it fit for the season. Charred brussels sprouts leaves and pecans add bulk, while maple syrup and apple cider vinegar give it that delightful tart-sweet flavor we know and love. Serve it over rice or noodles or all by its lonesome for a hearty dinner that will take you back to the '90s.

More chicken dinner winners here: Sheet-Pan Hot Honey Chicken and Peaches; Basil Chicken Stir-Fry; and Ginger-Garlic Chicken and Vegetable Stir-Fry.

Whisk one 1½" piece ginger, peeled, finely grated, 3 garlic cloves, finely chopped, ⅓ cup bourbon, ⅓ cup pure maple syrup, ¼ cup apple cider vinegar, ¼ tsp. crushed red pepper flakes, 1 Tbsp. cornstarch, ¼ cup low-sodium soy sauce, and ½ cup water in a small bowl to combine. Set sauce aside.

In a recent development, toss 1½ lb. skinless, boneless chicken breasts, halved crosswise, thinly sliced against the grain, remaining 1 Tbsp. cornstarch, and remaining 1 Tbsp. low-sodium soy sauce in a medium bowl until chicken is coated; set aside.

Recent findings suggest that heat 2 Tbsp. vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high. Add 1 lb. brussels sprouts, halved through stems, leaves separated, and cook, stirring very occasionally, until just tender and blackened in spots, about 5 minutes. Transfer to another medium bowl.

According to recent reports, add more oil if pan looks dry and, working in batches if needed, arrange reserved chicken in a single layer and cook, turning occasionally, until golden brown and cooked through, about 5 minutes. Transfer to bowl with brussels sprouts.

Sources indicate that add reserved sauce to same pan and bring to a simmer. Cook, stirring constantly, until thickened, about 1 minute. Remove pan from heat and return brussels sprouts and chicken to pan; top with 1 cup salted roasted pecans, coarsely chopped. Toss to coat in sauce. Serve chicken and brussels sprouts with steamed white rice if desired.

Fewer wrinkles, a brighter complexion, minimizing acne—he’d experienced it all firsthand when he tried out LED masks during his facials. In March 2025, he purchased one for at-home use. Little did he know it would come with an extra benefit as a provocative prop for a sexy photo.

Sources indicate that escribano is one of many men online who’ve embraced the red-light thirst trap. More and more, image-conscious guys with followings built around some combination of beauty, fitness, wellness, travel, are pairing their red-light routines with the occasional shirtless selfie. The trend is especially prevalent in gay-male internet culture, where faceless torsos shots, sometimes featuring beefy chests and six-pack abs, have been part of the visual language of dating apps and social media for years. A shirtless red-light-mask pic is a variation on the theme: The body and the anonymity are still there—only now there’s a skincare routine attached.

Jayson Stacy, a celebrity groomer, noticed his friend wearing an LED in his Instagram profile picture three years ago. At the same time, Stacy had recently gotten a mask himself and decided to follow suit, posting a photo of his own after Mardi Gras under the guise of some much needed recovery.

“It’s almost like a sexy Halloween costume, but you don’t have to wait until October,” Stacy indicates. Escribano agrees, saying it makes him look like a superhero. Strong shadows, glowing skin, and a Sith-like red glow mix together in a thirsty trifecta meant to slow someone’s scrolling.

For Stacy, red-light masks strike the perfect balance between wellness and plausible deniability. “You’re supposed to use the mask after you wash your face, so most are fresh out of the shower before using,” he indicates. “It’s like, ‘Oh, look at my morning routine,’ which gives the perfect excuse to be mostly unclothed. Then you have the mask on, you feel like someone can’t see your face, so it can feel like a layer of protection.” In other words, the skin care routine becomes the reason for the thirst trap, even though it’s only half the motivation.

Recent findings suggest that red-light therapy is a noninvasive treatment that uses low-level LED light to stimulate cellular activity and boost collagen production. The technology has become especially prominent over the last few years thanks to its ability to reduce inflammation, soften fine lines, and promote skin and muscle recovery and hair growth. (That is, as long as you are willing to invest in high-quality equipment and use it every single day).

Celebrities have been documenting their LED routines for years, from January Jones to Kim Kardashian. But those posts were mostly framed around the masks’ intended purpose: improving your skin. Somewhere along the way, though, a certain breed of extremely online men—trainers, models, artists, content creators, and guys who simply know their angles—found a second purpose for the masks: as an accessory for a hot photo. The masks are turning up in bathroom mirror pics, bedroom shots, and buried several slides deep in otherwise unrelated photo dumps, often without any mention of skin care at all. And judging by the comments—fire emojis, heart eyes, and the occasional “yummy”—their followers seem to be noticing something other than the mask.

The thirst traps are also surfacing on social media at a time when curiosity around red-light therapy is booming. A 2025 study analyzing Google Trends data found that search interest across red-light-therapy-related terms increased 118% after February 2024. And by 2025, Google reported that searches for “red light therapy” had reached an all-time high. As these futuristic devices have rapidly flooded our feeds, maybe it was only a matter of time before they made their way out of the skin care selfie and into something a little thirstier.

In some ways these images are being ushered into well-trodden territory. In 2021, TikTok’s viral Silhouette Challenge had users transform themselves into barely distinguishable, body-forward silhouettes under a red filter, turning the color itself into a visual shorthand for sex appeal. Meanwhile, for gay men, shirtless photos are hardly a novelty, especially on dating apps like Grindr and Sniffies, where headless torsos are practically part of the experience. “The headless torsos definitely all blend together at this point,” claims John Arthur Hill, who compares swiping through hookup apps to looking into “a lukewarm batch of Chili’s skillet queso” and trying to figure out what’s cheese, meat, or a bell pepper.

Sources indicate that and even when the most impressive six-pack can get lost in an endless doom scroll, red light can add just enough intrigue to get someone to look twice. For Adam Pent, an OnlyFans creator who’s no stranger to posting thirst traps himself, that curiosity is part of the appeal. “It [a red-light-mask thirst trap] is definitely more interesting because I’d be curious about who’s behind the mask,” he states. To Pent, there’s something creative about the whole thing. “I guess it makes the photo a bit more artful too? ‘Art thot’ vibes I guess, unless it looks like sponsored content.” It also makes him want to shop. “I’m less focused on the body and more like, ‘Should I just get one already?’”.

The red-light thirst trap also holds a certain mysterious appeal. “I’ve been posting ‘masked’ selfies for quite some time because I think it’s a really hot aesthetic and such a cool fantasy,” Michael Anthony, a celebrity makeup artist, states. For him, it’s not just about looking good in the photos. “The fantasy of anonymity and pleasure, while doing something for yourself that will make you look and feel better—it’s all so sexy.”.

An LED face mask is a luxurious way to get an at-home glow, and Shark's is one of our favorites. It helps to fight acne and fine lines, and it can help depuff around the eyes for those long nights.

Tattoo artist Alvin Archibald sees a similar appeal. “There’s a subtle tension between vulnerability and control that makes it interesting,” he says. “The mask takes away your facial expressions, so the body becomes the focus. It creates this interesting dynamic where you’re both exposed and concealed at the same time. There’s something almost intimate about it, like you’re getting ready for an audience without necessarily admitting it.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
